Soundness on the planted cases: a write the frontend cannot model is never dropped. Through (a local alias of &a.X) writes X := [param, v] exactly; Leak (&a.Y passed to a dynamic call) writes Y with a havoc value (holding [unknown, ...]); Deref (a write through a pointer read from the state) writes every family (P, X, Y) with havoc values; Fill (writes inside a loop bounded by an argument) writes Arr and N with havoc values and records loop debt, and K := 7 after the loop exactly; Go (a goroutine writing X) writes X with a havoc value, records goroutine debt, and Z := 2 exactly.

The KV-store pattern: the planted Keeper (a field of an interface type with Get/Has/Set/Delete over []byte keys) has the mapping family store; its actions are Balance, Remove, SetBalance; SetBalance writes store at a map key that holds [param, addr] and the prefix constant [str, hex("bal/")], with a value that mentions [param, amt], behind a guard over [param, caller]; Remove deletes (writes 0) at that key behind a guard that reads [storage, store].

thresholds.opaque: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: a typed-sorts sidecar names "types_fallback": "opaque" (the only value; anything else is refused). Without the key nothing changes: holon types refuses the milestone on an ill-sorted term (exit 2, nothing written), as N2 says. Under the key, holon types types each document of the sidecar on its own, in sorted order. A document whose typed model generation raises the ill-sorted error is OPAQUE: (O1) it is a recorded miss, one entry of gen/<M>/sorts/opaque.json {document, sha256, model, term, reason}, where term is the action and the operation named by the error (its first clause, before ': ') and reason is the error's whole text, which names the operation and its source span; the miss is never silent and the composed row counts it (types_opaque). (O2) Its STATE: it has no typed model, so no state variable of it exists in any model; nothing constrains it. (O3) Its ACTIONS: none is modelled; no law of any rule is derived over it (typed part, DISCH, FACT, UNDO, SORT, SYM), so every claim over it is UNKNOWN (counted at the document: one miss). (O4) What OTHER documents may assume about it: nothing new. Every typed model is one document's: another contract is reached only through an external call, whose answer is a free value (A-env) whether or not the callee is typed, so a typed document's model, laws and verdicts do not depend on whether an opaque document is in the milestone, apart from the milestone-wide assignment hash the model's header comment names (and so its model_sha256). (O5) Every stage after types (model, disch, derive, run) reads the typed documents only: the sidecar's documents minus the opaque ones; the sort pass and types read every document. The sort assignment is the sort pass's over all documents, unchanged. (O6) A taint violation (G4) still refuses the milestone, and an error that is not the ill-sorted one (an unreadable input) still exits 1. (O7) If every document is opaque, holon types writes types.json with no model and exits 0; the later stages then have no document and derive no typed law.
thresholds.soundness: Opacity only removes: an opaque document contributes no model, no state constraint, no action and no law, and it changes no typed document's model (O4). So the set of laws decided under the fallback is a subset of the laws the same milestone would decide without that document, each with the same verdict. No law can be PROVED or REFUTED through an opaque document.
thresholds.amendment_to_brief: The coordinator's relay of the lead's corrected rulings Q77 and Q78 (read before this commit): the torsor-role search is part (2) of this key, under Q74 (1)-(3) and (5); any cutoff is a preregistered tier under Q75 and Q76. thresholds.search: Part (2), fixed here before any build commit. The search decides, for one affine component, whether the classes' role domains (subsets of {P, G}) admit an assignment satisfying every ternary table (+: (P,G,P) (G,P,P) (G,G,G); -: (P,P,G) (P,G,P) (G,G,G)); with P = 1 and G = 0 each table is 'out = lhs + rhs' or 'lhs = rhs + out' with no carry, a 1-in-3-type relation, so the problem is NP-complete with seeds and exponential in the worst case under any exact strategy. The old strategy (I110) propagates (generalized arc consistency), then branches on the least open variable, chronologically. On a network whose leftover parts are independent, a part that fails is re-discovered under every combination of choices in the parts sorted before it: exponential thrashing. The rewrite, D1: after each propagation, the constraints that hold a variable with more than one role left are grouped by the connected components of those variables; a constraint with every variable decided is satisfied (propagation left it a supporting row) and drops out; with two or more parts, the network is satisfiable iff every part is, each searched on its own (in order of its least open variable, stopping at the first that fails); with one part, the old branching is unchanged. D1 is an evaluation strategy only: _search returns the same boolean on every input, so the satisfiable verdict, every role set (Component.roles), role pair and difference sort, and so every sort output, are the same. Which roles are admissible is never changed. The flag holon.sorts.solve.DECOMPOSE (True; False is the old strategy) exists for the identity test only. No new cutoff and no new tier: the sort budget's tier stays I110's 5,000,000. The units keep I110's definition (one search node, one table row a propagation sweep reads, ...); D1's own scan of a node's constraints is not metered (one pass over the constraints that the same node's propagation reads at least three rows of each, so time stays within a constant factor of the metered work).

thresholds.counting: Q80, Q76, Q69: the counted run is the first measured run of holon eval holon --protocol spec/M6/lib/i112_run.json --compose over the corpus that finishes; every prediction is scored on it. A re-run counts only if the first attempt never finished; any other re-run is reported beside it as not counted. No tier is added. The lead's correction to Q80 (relayed before this prereg): no started run's output is ever deleted, counted or not; a run that extracts nothing, fails or is abandoned keeps its output, recorded or vaulted under Q56, and is reported.
thresholds.routing: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: the protocol names run_routing "per_runner". Without it the driver's run step is I110's two calls, unchanged. Under it, holon.eval.holon_run.route(derivation) groups the derived law ids, each by its laws/<M>/DERIVATION.json entry: disch: rule DISCH with a sub-form of holon.disch.run.SUBFORMS; fact: rule FACT; typed: rule SORT with sub-form as_member, realize or reinterpret, and rules UNDO and SYM; milestone: every other law (PAR and every route C family). Each non-empty group is one `holon run --milestone M --laws <ids> --out results/M --gen-dir gen/M` call, in the order disch, fact, typed, milestone, with only its runner's arguments: disch --sidecar <typed> --disch <disch> --section-errors unknown (when the protocol names disch.section_errors); fact --sidecar <typed> --fact-sidecar <fact>; typed --sidecar <typed>; milestone none. A call that fails is recorded (its exit) and the next one runs. A law with no record after every call is UNKNOWN with no record. The stage detail holds aggregates only (per runner: laws, status, exit, records, section errors).
thresholds.section_errors: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: `holon run ... --section-errors unknown` (holon.disch.run). Without it a holon.disch.section.SectionError raised while building one document's DISCH section propagates and stops the runner, as before. Under it, when building a document's section (holon.disch.run.Doc) raises SectionError, that document's section is in error: every DISCH law the run names whose facts document is that document gets a record with status UNKNOWN, kernel verdict not_run, checker not_run, no witness, attempts [{kind: section, error: <the error's text>}] and bound "the DISCH section of <model> is refused: <the error's text>"; no candidate, proof or search is attempted for it, so an error never yields PROVED or REFUTED. Every other document's section is built and its laws decided as before; S3's neighbourhood seeds are taken from the laws of the same document only (unchanged), so another section's error changes no verdict of a section without one. Only SectionError is caught: any other exception still stops the runner.
thresholds.opaque_classes: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit; Q81). Opt-in only: a typed-sorts sidecar under types_fallback "opaque" names types_opaque_classes, a non-empty sorted subset of ["gen_error", "member_layout", "unsupported"]; any other value is refused when the sidecar is read, and the key without types_fallback is refused. Absent, the classes are ["gen_error"] and every output is I111's byte for byte. A document's typed model generation that raises holon.sorts.model3.GenError, whatever the GenError (the lead's correction to Q81, relayed before this prereg: not only I111's ill-sorted case; I111's code already catches every GenError, so this names its class), is class gen_error; holon.machine.MemberLayoutError (a ModelError subclass raised exactly where holon.machine refuses a field whose slot or offset is not the compiler's member layout of its family's type, the refusal I111 recorded; its text is unchanged) is class member_layout; holon.extracted_eval.Unsupported is class unsupported. A document is opaque when its error's class is named; each miss then also records class (only when the sidecar names types_opaque_classes). I111's O2-O7 are unchanged: no model, no state, no action, no law; every later stage reads the typed documents only. A milestone-wide input error stays a refusal of the milestone: the assignment, the sidecar, the seeds or the binding unreadable (exit 1), a taint violation (exit 2), and every other exception, ModelError included (a family's slot or offset not in the compiler's layout at all, a document that cannot be loaded), refuse the milestone as before.
thresholds.withhold: (3) holon_run.withhold, which runs on every composed row (the --roles opt-in), also removes from the committed output every file under <id>/gen/ whose path or text names a law id the entry derived (kept in the vault under withheld_gen/), recorded as <id>/gen_withheld.json {files, sha256} (I111's tool's canonical form), and replaces every law id inside a stage's detail with "<law id withheld>". The run stage's detail (per_runner) is aggregates only. After it, no committed file of the entry names a derived law id, and no record, verdict or witness is committed.
thresholds.preflight: (4) Q80. Under the protocol's preflight "toolchain_sets", holon eval holon checks, before any entry runs, every binary of config/toolchains.json its protocol can select (solidity.compiler.version "pragma": every solc_set release, the file <dir>/solc-<v> present with the pinned sha256; go.toolchain "go_directive": every go_set release, its go binary present and printing the pinned version_line, the go_set pinning tarballs rather than binaries). Any missing or different: exit 2, nothing written, the failures named on stderr. Otherwise corpus.json records preflight {status: ok, solc: {checked, ok}, go: {checked, ok}, binaries: [{tool, version, path, sha256 or version_line, ok}]}.
thresholds.soundness: (1) routing changes which process decides a law, never how: each runner decides its laws as it does when holon run is called on them alone. A section error yields UNKNOWN with no attempt, so it can only remove decisions. (2) opacity under the new classes is I111's O2-O4: the document contributes no model, state, action or law, so it only removes constraints. (3) and (4) decide nothing.

I115.title: I115: the binding wall (HUMAN_ANSWERS Q88 (2), Q87): (1) the milestone runner checks each law's binding (the kernel cone of its statement over its model) before deciding it, and a law that cannot be bound is UNKNOWN with the error (holon run --unbound unknown; protocol run_unbound "unknown"); the composed route binds its own milestone with holon bind over the derived statements (protocol bind "derived"; holon bind --unbound skip), and a binding check admits a decided record only when its law is bound with the record's statement hash and model; (2) Q87: every go_set release pins its installed bin/go sha256 and the preflight checks it (protocol preflight_go "bin_sha256"), a refusal recorded. Run through holon eval holon --compose with I112's protocol plus the three opt-ins

thresholds.doc: No number is a gate (BUILD_PLAN §4, M6 exit). Each prediction holds or misses as stated; a miss is reported, never forced. P1-P6 are on planted fixtures (tests_m6/fixtures/i115) and unit inputs. P7-P10 are smoke measures on I51's corpus, contaminated by I51, I103-I112 and I107. P11 is a measurement on I106's targets, contaminated: post-I107. I114 scores generality on the sealed pair. Laws are reported as aggregates only, never splitting PROVED from REFUTED (Q56, Q89); stage reasons only for stages before any decision (Q72).
thresholds.instruments: spec/M6/lib/i115_run.json (the run protocol: I112's plus run_unbound "unknown", bind "derived" and preflight_go "bin_sha256"; the tier typed.sort_budget is I110's 5000000, unchanged) and tests_m6/test_i115_binding_wall.py (every check)
thresholds.base: claude/i112-run-wall at a5db40d6 (I112, #190 not yet landed); the lead's I112 landing is merged by a merge commit before the first measured run
thresholds.baseline: I112's counted composed run (results/M6/I112/holon/corpus.json): entries ok at extract 14, sorts 14, types 14, model 14, disch 14, derive 14, run 0; 107 laws derived, 1 decided (PROVED and REFUTED together, Q56); the milestone runner wrote 0 records for its 93 PAR laws (a BindingError in holon.codecrun.decide stops the runner: holon.bindings.kernel_cone, a statement naming a Go-op definition the component's model leaves out)
thresholds.diagnosis: Found on the planted fixture before this prereg (tests_m6/fixtures/i115, reproduced at the base): the Go-op model (holon.gen.goloop) models an op only in its loop class (one loop body over the carrier's cells); any other op is Unsupported, its definitions ok_<op> and <op> are not generated, and goloop.decide leaves the laws naming it UNKNOWN. holon.codecrun.decide then computes the law's kernel cone over that model (for the deps index and the record), kernel_cone raises BindingError (M.ok_<op> resolves to no kernel entry), and the exception stops the whole milestone runner, so no law of the run gets a record, the decidable ones included. The binding route A's milestones get from spec/bindings is never made either: the composed route runs no holon bind, so G2 could not check any decided law of it.
thresholds.counting: Q80, Q76, Q69: the counted run is the first measured run of holon eval holon --protocol spec/M6/lib/i115_run.json --compose over the corpus that finishes; every prediction is scored on it. A re-run counts only if the first attempt never finished; any other re-run is reported beside it as not counted. No started run's output is ever deleted. The preflight (I112's plus Q87's go pins) must pass before it.
thresholds.unbound: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: holon run ... --unbound unknown (holon.mpipeline's run and holon.codecrun.decide; the composed driver passes it to the milestone runner under protocol run_unbound "unknown"). Without it every output is as before, and a BindingError stops the runner as before. Under it, before a law of the milestone runner is decided, its binding is computed: the kernel cone (holon.bindings.kernel_cone) of the law's statement roots (holon.records.ir_roots_text) over the kernel entries of the model the law is decided over. If that raises holon.bindings.BindingError, nothing is attempted for the law: its record has status UNKNOWN, kernel verdict not_run, checker not_run, no witness, no law or proof file, attempts [{kind: binding, error: <the error's text>}] and bound "not decided: the statement cannot be bound to its model: <the error's text>"; its deps entry has an empty cone. If the cone of the decided statement text (after the decision) raises BindingError, the decision is dropped the same way (status UNKNOWN, its law and proof files removed). Every other law is decided as before. Only BindingError is caught.
thresholds.bind: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: protocol bind "derived". After the run step, the composed driver runs holon bind --milestone M --root <scratch root> --unbound skip (stage bind): every derived law is bound by holon.bindings.bind_law, as route A's milestones are, into the scratch root's spec/bindings/<M>.json (written fresh: the scratch root's copy of spec/bindings holds no <M>.json, and nothing is written to the repository's spec/bindings); a law whose bind_law raises BindingError is left out and listed in spec/bindings/<M>.unbound.json {law id: error}. --unbound skip is refused on a milestone whose spec/bindings/<M>.json already exists (an existing binding only changes through the statement lifecycle, unchanged). Then the binding check (holon.eval.holon_run.binding_check): a PROVED or REFUTED record is admitted only when its law is bound and the binding's statement_hash equals the record's statement_hash and the binding's model equals the record's artifacts.model; any other decided record is rewritten UNKNOWN (kernel and checker not_run, witness and difference null, artifacts laws and proof null, attempts + [{kind: binding_check, error}], bound "not decided: the binding check refuses the record: <why>"). An UNKNOWN record is left as it is. No family is exempt: every derived law, whatever its runner, goes through holon bind and the check (G2 binds every law of a milestone: holon.bindings.derive over ir.load_laws_any). The stage's detail holds aggregates only: laws, bound, unbound, decided records refused. The bindings and the unbound list name law ids, so they go to the vault (Q56) and are never copied into the committed output.
thresholds.go_pins: (2) Q87. config/toolchains.json: each go_set release gains bin_sha256, the sha256 of its installed bin/go (1.24.7: /usr/local/go/bin/go, the go on PATH; 1.25.14: <goroot>/bin/go as tools/install_toolchain_sets.sh installs it from the pinned tarball). Under protocol preflight "toolchain_sets" with preflight_go "bin_sha256", the preflight checks every go_set release's bin/go present, its sha256 equal to bin_sha256 (a release without bin_sha256 fails) and its version line equal to version_line; any failure refuses the run: exit 2, the refusal recorded in <out>/preflight.json (the preflight with status failed and every binary checked) and nothing else written. Without preflight_go (I112's protocol) the go check is the version line alone, unchanged: I112's basis stands for I112's run.
thresholds.soundness: (1) The binding check can only remove decisions: a law that cannot be bound is UNKNOWN with nothing attempted; a decided record the binding check refuses is rewritten UNKNOWN; no record is ever made PROVED or REFUTED by it. A law that can be bound is decided exactly as before (the same decider, the same model). The bindings are holon bind's own (holon.bindings.bind_law, unchanged), over the scratch root. (2) decides nothing.

predictions.claim: (1) holon run --unbound unknown, unit level on the planted fixture tests_m6/fixtures/i115 (the composed route's typed part and route C under spec/M6/lib/i115_run.json): the milestone runner exits 0 and writes a record for each of its laws; the totality law over Counter's Bump (an op the Go-op model leaves out) is UNKNOWN with exactly one attempt, kind binding, and no witness; at least one PAR law over Blob is decided. Without --unbound (I112's protocol) the milestone runner exits non-zero with a BindingError and the Counter law has no record.

(1) The bind stage on the planted fixture: stage bind ok; spec/bindings/M9.json (the scratch root's) binds every derived law but the Counter totality law, which is the only entry of spec/bindings/M9.unbound.json; bound plus unbound equals derived; every PROVED or REFUTED record passes the binding check (its law bound with its statement hash and model), and no record the check admits is UNKNOWN by it; the repository's spec/bindings is unchanged.

(1) The planted control of the binding check, unit level (holon_run.binding_check over a planted milestone directory): a REFUTED record whose law is missing from the bindings, one whose binding names another model, and one whose binding's statement hash differs are each rewritten UNKNOWN with an attempt kind binding_check; a correctly bound PROVED record and an UNKNOWN record are left byte-identical. holon bind --unbound skip refuses (exit 1) when spec/bindings/<M>.json exists.

(1) No family is routed around the binding: every derived law of the planted run (DISCH and PAR) is in the bindings or the unbound list, and the DISCH records are unchanged by the check. Every derived record carries roles_source (the composed row's laws, before withholding).

(2) Q87: every go_set release of config/toolchains.json has bin_sha256; under the I115 protocol the preflight passes on a planted set whose bin/go matches, and refuses (exit 2) when a bin/go's sha256 differs or a release has no bin_sha256, recording the refusal in <out>/preflight.json (status failed) and writing nothing else; under I112's protocol the same planted sets are checked by version line alone (I112's results unchanged).

(1) Without the opt-ins every output is as before: I112's protocol names none of run_unbound, bind, preflight_go; holon run without --unbound on Morph's milestones is untouched (TestRegressions, P12).

(Corpus) holon eval holon --protocol spec/M6/lib/i115_run.json --compose, the counted run: the preflight is recorded ok with the go pins (go checked 2, ok 2); entries whose stage is ok at least extract 14, sorts 14, types 14, model 14, derive 14, and bind ok on every entry that derives a law; the run stage ok (every runner exits 0) on at least 5 of the 6 entries that derive laws in I112's run.

(Corpus) the milestone runner: every one of its laws gets a record (records = laws on every entry); at least 80 of its laws are UNKNOWN by the binding (their Go-op op outside goloop's loop class, attempt kind binding), aggregated; the binding check refuses no decided record.

(Corpus) laws as aggregates (Q56, Q89; never PROVED split from REFUTED): at least 100 derived, at least 1 decided, derived = decided + unknown per family; PAR laws decided: at most 5 (the corpus's Go ops are rarely in goloop's loop class); per-law rows withheld.
(Corpus, Q56) no committed file under results/M6/I115/holon names a law id; no bindings or unbound list is committed; every entry with laws has a laws_bundle_sha256.

(Spent targets, contaminated: post-I107) through --compose with --vault: no law is derived on either target (this key changes no stage before the run: EigenLayer stops at evidence and derive, Aave V3 at disch, as I112 measured), so Q88 (1)'s gate is not met by this key's counted runs (corpus decided at least 1, spent targets 0); aggregates only, one bundle commitment per target.

Morph moves only by re-stamp: no M0-M3 sidecar names run_unbound, bind or preflight_go; every JSON under results/M0-M3 and laws/M0-M3 equals the lead's once generator_sha256 and every seconds are removed (G1_EXCLUDED skipped). The gates M0, M1, M2 and partial M3 and holon land dirty are run locally and reported.
